blocks.text: Docker captures stdout/stderr through a logging driver; the default `json-file` doesn't rotate unless configured, so chatty containers can fill the disk and take down everything on the host.
Put that in `/etc/docker/daemon.json` and restart dockerd. Per service in Compose:

blocks.text: Logging settings apply only to containers created after the change: recreate existing ones (`up -d --force-recreate`).
Blocking (default): a slow log backend blocks the app's stdout writes and can stall the API. `mode: non-blocking` + `max-buffer-size` avoids stalls but may drop lines.

Q: "A host ran out of disk and the culprit is a container log. How do you prevent it?" A: "Switch the daemon default to the local driver or set json-file max-size/max-file, recreate containers so they pick it up, add disk alerts, and have apps log structured JSON to stdout for the platform to ship."

items: Log to stdout; let the driver handle retention.
